newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - BRL Hardy says targets 2nd half growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - BRL Hardy says targets 2nd half growth.

text.p: Vintner BRL Hardy Ltd said on Thursday it was targetting similar growth in the second half of calendar 1996 to that achieved in the first half.
The company earlier reported a 21 percent rise in operating profit to A$13.33 million for the six months to June 30.

"We are certainly targetting that sort of continuation but I think it is a brave man that says a result so outstanding can necessarily be maintained," managing director Stephen Millar told a news conference. "But we will maintain a very good result and it is certainly not beyond the realms of possibility (that) we can maintain that."
Asked if the full year would see another record result, Millar said: "There is no doubt about that...it will certainly be very significant.

Millar said total sales growth would probably be under the 12 percent increase achieved in 1995 as a result of the loss of the Cooper Beer agency and significantly reduced market share in fruit juice concentrate in Japan.

"We will exceed last year's sale growth in wine...but if you take something like A$12 million out on two odd bits, that is a significant amount, about four percent, (and) we will probably be under (overall)."
However, chairman John Pendrigh noted that the beer business was an agency line with very low margins.
Asked if the full year result depended on higher wine prices, Pendrigh said: "No, its dependent on a greater volume of sales of a bigger margin product."
BRL Hardy warned that the grape surpluses, especially in white varieties over the next two years could result in significant price competition in the domestic market.
However Millar said the price pressures would not impact on BRL Hardy bottom line.
"Quite the reverse, at worst case scenario we can maintain our margins," he said.

"If we manage it well, we can actually increase our margins because there is no doubt that come the 1997 vintage, premium varietal white grape prices are going to drop and that is an opportunity," he said.
Millar said the company was still seeking acquisitions and would prefer "big fish".

He said the company considered Orlando Wyndham, subject to recent sale speculation by its French-based owners Pernot Ricard, was not on the market and that given two recent takeovers in Australia, private companies probably offered the more likely opportunities.
